title: Workload Transferability and Quantized Benchmarks Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the process, tooling, and acceptance criteria for evaluating how well a candidate model (and its quantized variants) transfers across Redwood workloads. It combines: the eval-harness workload simulator, curated prompt sets, a lightweight quantization profile, and a triage path for regressions discovered during pre-production rollouts. The goal is to produce deterministic pass/fail signals and prioritized remediation actions for the Platform and Model Onboarding teams.

Scope

- Applies to any model being considered for: Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Focuses on transferability metrics (latency distribution, response quality per prompt cohort, token-efficiency), plus quantization stability (delta in quality when using int8/4 schemes).
- Not intended for large-scale user AB tests (those are handled by product experimentation teams).

Components

1) Eval Harness services
- eval-scheduler: schedules runs, shards prompts, and stores artifacts to object-storage (s3://redwood-evals).
- eval-runner: containerized runner (image: ghcr.io/redwood/eval-runner:v2.3) that executes model calls against the serving runtime under controlled load.
- eval-aggregator: aggregates per-prompt signals and computes cohort-level metrics.

2) Prompt and benchmark catalog
- Prompt cohorts: conversational-support, search-rewrite, code-completion, multi-turn-dialog. Each cohort has 500–2,000 prompts depending on domain coverage.
- Stress bench: latency-sensitive subset (N=200) and quality-sensitive subset (N=500).

3) Quantization profiles
- A canonical YAML profile (example below) specifying quant bits, per-layer overrides, and authorized kernel fallbacks. Profiles are versioned in the repo: git@github.com:redwood/quant-profiles.git

4) Transferability test matrix
- Workload axes: request size distribution (short/medium/long), concurrency (1, 8, 64), presence of KV-cache warm start.
- Variant axes: fp16 baseline, int8 symmetric, int4 advanced, 8-bit with per-channel scales.

Acceptance criteria and SLOs

- Latency SLO (regional-hosted): median < 60 ms for short prompts under concurrency=8; p95 < 250 ms.
- Quality SLOs: BLEU/ROUGE/CodeBLEU or model-specific eval metrics must degrade by <= 2.5% relative to fp16 baseline for targeted cohort averages.
- Quantization stability: for int8 baseline, no more than 5% of prompts may flip from acceptable->unacceptable classification (binary acceptability labels maintained in the prompt catalog).
- Cost delta guardrail: expected per-token cost improvement from quantization must be >= 15% to consider rollout.

Workflows

A) New-model onboarding: transferability checklist (owner: model-onboarding team)
1. Create an eval-run entry via CLI and include: model artifact sha, quant profile sha, target workloads.
   - CLI: ri-eval create --model sha:abcdef --profile v1.2 --workloads short,med,long --name "gptx-transfer-test"
2. Run baseline fp16 across all workloads: ri-eval run --id <id> --variant baseline-fp16 --concurrency 1,8,64
3. Run quantized variants: append --variant int8,int4 --profile-sha <sha>
4. Wait for aggregator completion; review artifact link in the eval dashboard.
5. Verify acceptance criteria above. If all pass, record sign-off in the onboarding checklist and schedule canary traffic (see rollout checklist).

B) Regression triage (when a regression signal is detected in CI or preproduction)
1. Triage owner (oncall-model) assigns severity: Sev3 (minor) | Sev2 (degrades metric > 3%) | Sev1 (p95 latency >500 ms / severe quality regressions).
2. Reproduce with deterministic seed: ri-eval run --id <id> --replay --seed 42 --exact-prompts
3. Compare per-prompt diffs using the aggregator delta report: delta_report.csv includes columns: prompt_id, baseline_metric, variant_metric, relative_change, acceptability_change.
4. If acceptability_change flagged for >10 prompts: stop rollout and trigger model rollback.
5. If regression is latency-only and confined to a kernel: open issue in infra-kerneleth repo, attach flamegraph and profiler output (see Profiling checklist below).

Profiling checklist (runtime/serving)

- Capture a 30-second p95 spike window with tracing enabled: curl -X POST $TRACE_COLLECTOR/api/capture --data '{"trace_id":"<trace>"}'
- Collect GPU metrics: nvidia-smi dmon --delay 4 --count 15 > gpu-dmon.out
- Run lightweight sampling profiler (rbpf): /opt/redwood/profiler/sample --pid <pid> --duration 20s > sample.prof
- Gather KV-cache hit rate and batch size histograms from runtime metrics (metrics key: runtime.request.kv_hit_ratio, runtime.request.batch_size_hist)

Quantization profile example (canonical YAML)

---
profile_name: "fast-int8-transfer-001"
description: "Default int8 profile tuned for transferability tests; fallback to fp16 for layer types: embedding, layernorm"
global_bits: 8
per_layer_overrides:
  - layer_pattern: "embedding*"
    bits: 16
  - layer_pattern: "layernorm*"
    bits: 16
fallback_policy:
  kernel_fallbacks: ["fp16", "jit-specialized"]
  max_abs_error_threshold: 1e-3
---

Example aggregator output (CSV columns)

prompt_id,cohort,baseline_score,variant_score,score_delta,baseline_accept,variant_accept
0001,conversational-support,0.92,0.89,-0.03,1,1
0021,code-completion,0.76,0.61,-0.15,1,0

Decision and rollout guidance

- If all SLOs and guardrails meet criteria: proceed to canary stage (traffic split 1% -> 5% -> 20% with 24h stability windows). Use rollout policy: canary-duration=24h, rollback-on=any-sev2+ event.
- If quality fails but cost savings > 30%: consider hybrid route (deploy quantized variant behind cost-sensitive route and keep fp16 default). Document route in routing-policies page.
